title: Roth's Theorem via Triangle Removal (Corners Reduction)
description: Explicit reduction from Roth's theorem to the corners theorem via the construction S = {(x,y) : 2x+y ∈ A}, showing corners in S correspond to 3-APs in A

meta.author: Roth/Ruzsa-Szemerédi (formalized in Lean 4)
originalContributions: Proved corners in S ↔ 3-APs in A (both directions, verified)
Demonstrated why the coefficient 2 uniquely gives 3-APs
Injectivity of the parameterization map (a,x) ↦ (x, a-2x)
meta.assumptions: 2 axioms: (1) cornerSet_card -- density preservation |S| = |A|·N, provable by the injective parameterization (a,x) ↦ (x, a-2x). (2) roth_via_corners -- the final Roth theorem via corners, derivable from Mathlib's corners theorem + density preservation.

overview.historicalContext: Roth proved his theorem on 3-APs in 1953 using Fourier analysis. The alternative proof via the triangle removal lemma was discovered by Ruzsa and Szemerédi (1978). The key insight is that 3-AP problems can be encoded as corner problems in Z/NZ × Z/NZ, which in turn reduce to the triangle removal lemma via the regularity method.
overview.problemStatement: **Roth via Corners**: Given A ⊆ Z/NZ with |A| ≥ δN, construct S = {(x,y) : 2x+y ∈ A} and show that corners in S correspond to 3-APs in A.
overview.text: Explicit reduction from Roth's theorem to the corners theorem via the corner set construction
overview.proofStrategy: Define cornerSet A = {(x,y) ∈ (Z/NZ)² : 2x+y ∈ A}. A corner (x,y), (x+d,y), (x,y+d) in S gives 2x+y, 2x+y+d, 2x+y+2d ∈ A (a 3-AP). Conversely, each 3-AP {a, a+d, a+2d} in A yields N corners in S. The corners theorem then gives Roth.
keyInsights: The coefficient 2 in '2x+y' is the unique coefficient that makes corners correspond to 3-APs: cx+y with c=1 gives sum triples, c=3 gives {a,a+d,a+3d}, only c=2 gives {a,a+d,a+2d}.
Each 3-AP produces N corners (one for each base point x), providing a quantitative amplification from APs to corners.
The AP-free ⇒ corner-free direction is the key reduction: it converts the additive combinatorics problem (no 3-AP) into a geometric problem (no corner) solvable by the regularity method.

sections.title: Corner Set Construction
sections.summary: Definition of cornerSet A as {(x,y) : 2x+y ∈ A} with membership simp lemma.
sections.mathContext: The factor of 2 in 2x+y ensures that corners in S correspond to 3-APs rather than sum triples.

sections.title: Corners ↔ 3-AP Correspondence
sections.summary: Verified correspondence in both directions: corner_to_ap (corner gives 3-AP) and ap_to_corner (3-AP gives corners). Plus the contrapositive: AP-free implies corner-free.
sections.mathContext: The correspondence uses only ring arithmetic in ZMod N. The key equations are: 2(x+d)+y = (2x+y) + 2d and 2x+(y+d) = (2x+y) + d.

sections.title: Density Preservation
sections.summary: Injectivity of (a,x) ↦ (x, a-2x) proved. Density |S| = |A|·N axiomatized.
sections.mathContext: Each element a ∈ A has N preimages under the projection 2x+y, giving |S| = |A|·N.

sections.title: Roth from Corners
sections.summary: Full chain: Regularity → Triangle Removal → Corners → (this file) → Roth. Final theorem axiomatized.
sections.mathContext: The explicit corners reduction makes visible how the graph-theoretic machinery (regularity + triangle removal) applies to the number-theoretic problem.

crossReferences.description: The main gallery entry proves Roth via Fourier analysis (density increment). This entry provides the graph-theoretic proof via triangle removal.

conclusion.summary: Explicit formalization of the corners ↔ 3-AP correspondence that bridges the triangle removal lemma to Roth's theorem. Five theorems verified (corner_to_ap, ap_to_corner, apFree_imp_cornerFree, mem_cornerSet, cornerSet_map_injective), two axioms (density preservation, final theorem).
conclusion.implications: The corners approach generalizes: replacing 2x+y with kx+y gives k-term APs from 'k-dimensional corners'. This suggests a path to formalizing Szemerédi's theorem for general k via higher-dimensional hypergraph removal.
openQuestions: Can the density preservation axiom be eliminated by completing the bijection proof?
Can the connection to Mathlib's corners theorem be made explicit, eliminating the final axiom?
